If not completed, cleanup the worktree

observations.what: If commit_candidate fails, the exception is caught and candidate.error set, but the worktree is not cleaned up because candidate.completed is set to True only after successful commit. However, if commit_candidate raises an exception, it jumps to except, sets candidate.error, and then in finally, since candidate.completed is False (it was never set to True), cleanup_worktree is called. That is correct.

If terminate() raises an exception in the finally block, it will propagate and suppress any previous exception, potentially losing error information. However, the try-finally inside finally ensures cleanup_worktree is called even if terminate fails.
The branch name format uses uuid hex[:8] which is collision-prone in theory but acceptable for temporary branches.
